name: Toggl
summary: Time tracking and capacity planning for freelancers, consultants and agencies, with budgets, rates and profitability per project. Relaunched from Toggl Track to Toggl in 2026.
best_for: freelancers, consultants and agencies that bill by the hour and want frictionless tracking with budgets, rates and profitability per project
skip_if: you need surveillance-style monitoring (screenshots, activity scoring — deliberately not Toggl's philosophy), or free-tier tracking already covers you
honest_knock: Toggl's honesty problem is the good kind: the free tier is so capable that many teams never need to pay — the paid line is drawn exactly at 'do you bill clients' (budgets, rates, profitability). If you do, Starter earns itself fast; if you track time for personal discipline, resist the upgrade. Time tracking's real cost everywhere is adoption: the tool is frictionless, but the habit still has to be built.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month billed annually, or $12 monthly
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-09 and again 2026-10-01 on toggl.com/track/pricing, which now redirects to toggl.com/pricing) Free is $0 for a limited number of users and the page calls it free forever. Starter is $9 per user a month billed annually and $12 monthly; Premium is $16 annually and $24 monthly; Enterprise is quoted. The introductory $14 Premium rate renewing at $18 that we recorded in August is gone — Premium now carries one annual price. The billing toggle advertises 'Annual (Save 33.3%)' and '4 months free', which holds exactly for Premium but not for Starter, where $12 to $9 is 25%. Trial is 30 days; Enterprise adds volume discounts on annual and multiple workspaces under one organisation.
